# pcrecbench/tests/fixtures/ -- a small synthetic store for the reporter

Every record here is SYNTHETIC (`synthetic: true`, `note` says so,
`machine_id: "repfix-box"`, `run_id` prefixed `fixture-run-`). No engine
was ever run; every number was invented by hand specifically so the
reducer's arithmetic can be checked
(`pcrecbench/tests/test_report.py`'s `test_known_reduction` and
`test_set_grain_sums_per_subject_ns_per_call`). Nothing here may be
cited as a measurement. Generated by a scratch script (not committed;
lived at session scratch during development, current version
`gen_fixtures_v11.py`, superseding a schema-1.0-era `gen_fixtures.py`)
that writes every row -- including the deliberately-failing,
unsupported-by-declaration, gave-up and old-shaped ones -- directly, so
regenerating the FILES from an equivalent script reproduces them
exactly. The one exception: `test_report.py`'s documented
positive-control exercise temporarily mutated one value in the pcrec
record and then restored it from a pre-edit backup, not by re-running
the generator.

**Schema: v1.1** (this store was restamped when master's schema v1.1
merged, 2026-08-25 -- lane b2fix). Every v1.1-required field is present
throughout: per-row `seq` (dense 1..N over every row of a record, in
emission/list order); `run.clock_source` / `driver_build_flags` /
`driver_compiler`; `environment.load`/`occupancy` as before+after
objects with raw evidence (`loadavg_raw`, `sampled_at`, mpstat block);
`subjects[].sha256`; `calibration` on every timed row (every timed row
here has `iterations` > 1) -- deliberately UNDER target (elapsed_ns
values are tiny, for hand-computability), so every one carries a
`calibration_note` explaining the shortfall (schema v1.1's X21 escape
hatch), not a silently-invented number that would happen to clear it.
`environment.quiet_attestation` (removed in v1.1) is absent throughout.

The sub-bench they describe (`fixture-mini@1.0`) is INVENTED for this
suite only -- two tiny patterns (`p-digits` = `^[0-9]{3}$`, `p-word` =
`^[a-z]{3}$`), five subjects (`s-num-1`, `s-num-2`, `s-word-1`,
`s-mix-set`, `s-give-up-1`), two regimes (`match-compliance`,
`short-subject-search`). It is not the email specimen and not derived
from any real pcrec-bench sub-bench. `s-num-1` and `s-num-2`
deliberately share ONE cell -- (`p-digits`, `match-compliance`) -- for
every testee: every OTHER (pattern, regime) combination here has
exactly one subject, which would make `--grain set` (manager change
request, 2026-08-25: sum per-subject ns/call across the whole subject
set, per trial, then reduce over trials) indistinguishable from
`--grain subject` everywhere if this pair did not exist.

## Layout

- `store/` -- the MAIN fixture store, WITH `store/index.tsv` (exercises
  the index-based discovery path). Three testees over `fixture-mini@1.0`:
    - `pcrec_1.0.0-gdeadbee_vm-caps-simdna` (`compiled-aot`) -- every
      cell passes. Its match-compliance rows all carry `form:
      whole-subject` (v1.1, record_schema.md 5 ADDITIONS 3: pcrec has
      no end-anchored matching mode, so compliance runs against a
      SEPARATE `(?:pattern)\z` artifact, with its own compile rows,
      cost and trials -- present here alongside the normal `plain`
      compile rows/search-mode match rows for the same patterns).
      `p-digits`/`s-num-1`/`match-compliance` is the HAND-COMPUTED
      `--grain subject` cell `test_known_reduction` checks exactly
      (trials 100000/110000/90000 ns over 1000 iterations -> ns/call
      [100,110,90] -> median 100, min 90, max 110); its sibling
      `s-num-2` (ns/call [50,90,160]) makes `p-digits`/`match-compliance`
      the HAND-COMPUTED `--grain set` cell
      `test_set_grain_sums_per_subject_ns_per_call` checks (per-trial
      SUMS [150,200,250] -> median 200, min 150, max 250).
    - `libpcre2_10.46_interp-caps-simdna` (`interpretive`) -- the
      `p-word`/`s-word-1`/`match-compliance` cell is DELIBERATELY WRONG
      (`did-not-match-as-expected` on all 3 trials); its sibling
      `p-word`/`s-give-up-1`/`match-compliance` is a v1.1 ADDITION,
      `match_outcome: gave-up` on all 3 trials (the engine's own
      resource limit, record_schema.md 5 ADDITIONS 2 -- NOT a wrong
      answer). The two subjects share ONE (pattern, regime), so the
      `--grain set` cell for this testee has TWO failing subjects with
      TWO DIFFERENT reasons -- exactly what
      `test_set_grain_excludes_whole_set_when_any_subject_fails` checks
      (`n_gave_up == 3`, `n_wrong == 3`, each subject individually
      labelled). `p-word`/`s-word-1`/`match-compliance` also shares its
      (pattern, subject, regime) with pcrec's PASSING `form:
      whole-subject` cell for the same coordinates -- since `form` is
      NOT a ranking-group key (manager fix request, 2026-08-25;
      `test_expectation_failing_cell_is_excluded_from_ranking`), the two
      testees are in ONE group, and only libpcre2-interp's `plain` entry
      is excluded from it.
    - `libpcre2_10.46_jit-caps-simdna` (`eager-jit`) -- `p-word` is
      `unsupported-by-declaration` (a fictional declaration reason, purely
      to exercise the outcome and the "no cost for an unsupported
      pattern" rule) with no match rows for that pattern on this testee.
  Together: a compile-cost mix of `compiled-aot` and `interpretive`
  (plus `eager-jit` as a bonus third class), all three testees × 1
  sub-bench × 2 regimes, one wrong-answer cell, one gave-up cell, one
  unsupported-by-declaration cell, one `form: whole-subject` testee. The
  same shape also makes `p-digits`/`match-compliance` the fixture that
  proves `form` never splits a ranking table (manager fix request,
  2026-08-25): pcrec (`whole-subject`) and BOTH libpcre2 testees
  (`plain`) all pass that cell, so all three appear together in ONE
  ranking table at both grains, each carrying its own `form` column --
  `test_form_never_splits_the_ranking_table`. This shape already existed
  here (pcrec whole-subject, libpcre2 plain, same pattern/regime) from
  the earlier v1.1 restamp, so no fixture changes were needed for this
  fix -- only `report.py`'s ranking-group key and the tests that assumed
  the old (incorrect) per-form split.
  NOT covered by an end-to-end record here: a `lazy-jit` testee (none of
  these three is one) -- the corrected `_lazy_jit_derivation` (schema
  v1.1's `first-match-row-minus-steady-state`, keyed on the lowest
  `seq`) is instead unit-tested directly against hand-built row dicts,
  `test_lazy_jit_derivation_uses_lowest_seq_not_trial_one`; see that
  test's docstring for why.
- `store_walk_only/` -- ONE record (the pcrec one, byte-identical to
  `store/`'s copy), with NO `index.tsv`, to exercise the reporter's walk
  fallback over `store/records/`.
- `mixed_version/` -- TWO SEPARATE scenarios, each in its own
  subdirectory (manager, 2026-08-25: "a real 1.0-vs-1.1 minor pair PLUS
  the 2.0/X17 case") so querying one never accidentally exercises the
  other's refusal:
    - `major_mismatch/records/` -- a valid v1.1 record
      (`...20260825T110000Z.jsonl`) alongside a `schema_version: "2.0"`
      record (`...20260825T110500Z.jsonl`), otherwise identical in
      shape. The 2.0 file is **INTENTIONALLY schema-INVALID** -- this
      repo's schema only defines 1.1 (`schema/record.schema.json`'s
      `x-record-schema-version`), so there is no way to construct a
      genuinely-valid 2.0 record without extending the schema (out of
      this lane's scope). This mirrors the `[B2]` lane's own convention
      (`schema/examples/bad/x17-future-major-version.jsonl`): the
      file's `note` field says so, and `test_all_fixtures_validate`
      asserts it is rejected by rule X17, not just "rejected". Exercises
      the reporter's mixed-MAJOR-version refusal
      (`test_mixed_schema_versions_refused`).
    - `minor_pair/records/` -- a genuinely schema-1.0-SHAPED record
      (`...20260825T090000Z.jsonl`; pre-v1.1 content: no `seq`, no
      `calibration`, the OLD `load`/`occupancy` array-of-3-numbers
      shape, `quiet_attestation` present) alongside a real v1.1 record
      (`...20260825T090500Z.jsonl`). Both declare MAJOR `1` (`1.0` vs
      `1.1`), so this must NOT trigger the mixed-version refusal --
      instead the old-shaped file is now independently INVALID against
      the current (v1.1) schema (missing every v1.1-required field),
      demonstrating record_schema.md 4.1's own warning made concrete:
      "a 1.0-stamped file is NOT readable as 1.1". Exercises the
      ordinary per-record-invalidity path surviving a MINOR-only
      version spread (`test_minor_version_pair_not_refused`).
  `make check-report` validates only the VALID half of each subdirectory
  independently against `schema/validate.py` (see the Makefile target);
  the deliberately-invalid halves are validated (for REJECTION, by the
  specific rule expected) inside `test_all_fixtures_validate` instead.

## Editing

If a match/compile row's timing values change, the setup line's
`content_hash` must be restamped or `schema/validate.py` fails on rule
X6 (this is deliberate -- it is what caught an unplanned tamper during
this lane's own positive-control exercise, see
`test_report.py`'s `_POSITIVE_CONTROL_LOG`):

    python3 schema/validate.py --print-hash <file>

and patch the printed value into `content_hash.value`. Adding or
reordering ROWS also changes every row's `seq` (assigned by
emission/list order) and therefore the hash -- restamp after any such
edit too, not just a value change.

Maintenance: update this file when files are added/removed or change
role.
